title: GPU Chaos Day: Experimentation Catalog and Runbook
author: Maya R. Singh
content:
Summary:

This page documents the GPU Chaos Day program: a curated catalog of safe, repeatable experiments for validating Redwood Inference's GPU fleet, routing, and tenant-isolation controls. The goal is to exercise failure modes relevant to production SLOs and billing/fairness systems while maintaining clear guardrails, rollback paths, and automated detection.

Why we run GPU Chaos Days:
- Verify preemption and eviction handling across spot/ephemeral pools.
- Validate warm-pool replenishment and KV cache rehydration behavior.
- Exercise routing fallbacks (region/model-variant/capacity-tier).
- Detect regressions in batching, prefix cache, and latency SLOs.
- Test billing and tenant throttling fairness under degraded capacity.

Scope and frequency:
- Scope: multi-tenant GPU fleets backing hosted API and Dedicated pools only. Air-gapped private deployments excluded unless customer-approved.
- Cadence: monthly small-scope exercises; quarterly large-scope cross-region drills; ad-hoc for major runtime changes or model onboardings.

Ownership and roles:
- Run owner: Eng-Infra Runbook Squad (primary contact: runbook-owner@redwood.example.com)
- Experiment owner: service team that requested the experiment (e.g., serving-runtime, gpu-fleet, routing)
- Oncall: Eng-SRE paging channel (#eng-sre-oncall) and the designated chaos day oncall rotation.
- Observability lead: Eng-Platform (dashboard + tracing owner).

Preflight checklist (required before any experiment):
1) Approvals:
   - Product/Platform owner sign-off for scope and tenant impact.
   - SRE lead sign-off for monitoring and paging readiness.
2) Communication:
   - Slack notice in #platform-ops 48 hours prior; reminder 2 hours before.
   - Postmortem/intent in the experiment tracker (link to retrospective board).
3) Safety controls applied:
   - Circuit-breaker: experiment toggled via feature-flag (chaos-experiment-<id>) with immediate rollback API.
   - Blast radius limits: test on single region / 10% of warm pool / opt-in tenants only.
   - Billing throttle guard: global throttle if token-rate drops 3x or cost-per-token exceeds threshold.
4) Metrics baseline capture: collect 30m pre-experiment baseline for key metrics (latency P50/P90/P99, request success rate, tokens/sec, queue depth, cost/token).

Experiment catalog (safe-by-default templates) — each entry contains intent, hypothesis, steps, expected impact, metrics to watch, rollback criteria, and postmortem prompts.

A. Controlled Preemption Sweep (spot-gpu-evict-01)
- Intent: Validate tenant-level fairness and graceful degradation when spot nodes are reclaimed.
- Hypothesis: Warm-pool seeding + KV cache rehydration will keep P90 latency < 500ms for production tier with <1% error spike when 10% of spot capacity preempted gradually.
- Steps:
  1) Scope to region: us-west-2; pools: spot-priority-pool-03; tenants: canary-tenant-set-A (opt-in).
  2) Announce and start: toggle feature flag and enable eviction controller in dry-run for 2m.
  3) Eviction pattern: trigger gradual eviction in waves (2% every 3 minutes) using simulated preemption script (see CLI below).
  4) Monitor: latency dashboard (GPU Serving > Region > us-west-2), oncall channel.
  5) Terminate if rollback criteria met (see below).
- Rollback criteria (immediate abort):
  - P99 latency increases > 2x baseline for 5m
  - Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase for 3m
  - KV cache miss rate > 20% for 5m
- Postmortem prompts: tenant-experiences affected, warm-pool seeding interval adequacy, preemption-drainer tuning.

B. Warm-Pool Starvation Test (warm-pool-drain-02)
- Intent: Ensure warm pools are replenished within target time under sustained load.
- Hypothesis: For warm-pool target=150, if 40% of warm capacity is evicted, replenishment completes within 12 minutes without exceeding burst budget.
- Steps:
  1) Limit to dedicated pool tag: dedicated-fast-01; scope tenants: infra-test-accounts.
  2) Simulate long-running inference jobs to consume KV caches and hold GPUs for 5–20s per request.
  3) Force node removal via API (i.e., cordon+drain) for scheduled nodes to emulate node loss.
  4) Observe autoscaler logs, pool size metrics, and billing/credits usage.
- Success criteria: replenishment <= 12m and no tenant throttling events.
- Rollback: stop simulated load; uncordon one node if replenishment stalls.

C. Routing Fallback Exercise (route-fallback-03)
- Intent: Validate automatic model-variant fallback and cross-region routing when a model flavor is overloaded or evicted.
- Hypothesis: Routing policy will migrate 5% of requests to backup variant within 30s and maintain P90 latency degradation < 30%.
- Steps:
  1) Target a single model _m5-compat-v2_ in eu-west-1.
  2) Apply transient rate-limit to the variant to induce immediate backpressure.
  3) Watch the smart-routing logs for fallback events and verify that requests are routed to m5-compat-v2-quantized or region-eu-west-2 fallback tier.
- Metrics: fallback count, fallback latency delta, error counts on primary variant.

D. Network Egress Path Switch (egress-swap-04)
- Intent: Validate egress path failover and NAT gateway cold-start effects on inter-region KV fetches and model cache misses.
- Hypothesis: A NAT swap may cause bursty latency and transient TCP connection failures for up to 90s; overall success rate should remain > 99.5%.
- Steps:
  1) Change route table to prefer alternate egress path in a small VPC segment.
  2) Simulate traffic using locust scenario: mix of short (<200ms) and long (>2s) generation calls.
  3) Monitor TCP retransmits, DNS error counts, and model cache miss rate.
- Rollback: restore original route immediately if retransmits > 3x baseline for 5 minutes.

E. CI/CD GPU Image Canary (image-canary-05)
- Intent: Validate new GPU runtime image with mixed-precision kernels without impacting prod traffic.
- Hypothesis: Canary pool with image v2025-01 will match baseline throughput within 10% and not increase OOMs or kernel-timeouts.
- Steps:
  1) Create canary nodepool (tag: canary-image-2025-01) with 5 nodes.
  2) Deploy image using image-promo pipeline with runbook gate.
  3) Run the smoke test suite: a) model-load, b) inference latency, c) memory/thermal regressions.
  4) Promote to staged pools after 60m of green signals.
- Prometheus probe examples and CLI:
```
# Triggering eviction simulation (example)
redwoodctl chaos simulate-eviction --pool spot-priority-pool-03 --region us-west-2 --percent 2 --duration 3m

# Toggle chaos feature flag
redwoodctl feature-flags set chaos-experiment-spot-gpu-evict-01 true
```

Telemetry and dashboards (minimum required):
| Metric / Dashboard | Query / Location | Owner | Alert threshold | Notes |
|--------------------|------------------|-------|-----------------|-------|
| P90 latency (regional) | dashboards/serving/latency-regional | serving-runtime | > 750ms for 10m | Pager to #eng-sre |
| Request error rate (5xx) | dashboards/serving/errors | eng-sre | > 0.5% absolute increase | Auto-abort policy applies |
| KV cache miss rate | dashboards/cache/kv-miss | eng-platform | > 15% for 5m | Check redis/kv pods |
| Warm-pool size | dashboards/gpu/pools | gpu-fleet | < target - 25% for 10m | Investigate autoscaler logs |
| Network retransmits | dashboards/network/tcp | cloud-networking | > 3x baseline | Possible egress path problem |

CI/CD and Terraform considerations:
- Any experiment that changes node images, autoscaler policy, or network routing must be run through the canary pipeline and have an IaC PR with: 1) plan output pasted into PR, 2) test plan with expected metrics, 3) rollback terraform snippet.
- Use modular feature flags via terraform module: modules/chaos/feature-flag-toogle.tf (example pattern below).
- Minimal PR template checklist:
  - Describe blast radius and opt-in-tenants.
  - Attach preflight baseline screenshots / links.
  - Link to runbook and postmortem board.

Example Terraform snippet (pattern only):
```
module "chaos_flag" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/modules/chaos.git//feature-flag"
  name   = "chaos-experiment-spot-gpu-evict-01"
  enabled = false
  owners = ["eng-infra/runbook"]
}
```

Safety and rollback primitives (automated):
- Global abort integration: the feature-flag system exposes a single-turnoff endpoint that removes experiment permissions and signals running clients to stop.
- Health-based aborts: alertmanager webhooks trigger a cancel job if configured thresholds breach.
- Tenant-level opt-out: a tenant can be whitelisted from chaos tests via tenant metadata tag: chaos-opt-out=true.

Post-experiment procedure (required within 48 hours):
1) Quick incident log (within 2 hours): capture high-level timeline, immediate actions, and whether rollback triggered.
2) Full postmortem (within 48 hours): runbook author + experiment & observability owners. Include: metrics diffs, what failed/what worked, action items, and detection/alerting gaps.
3) Follow-up ticketing: create tasks for runtime fixes, autoscaler tuning, or observability additions and assign priority (P0/P1/P2).

Playbook appendix: useful commands and dashboards
- redwoodctl chaos status --list
- redwoodctl pools describe --region us-west-2 --name warm-pool-*
- dashboards: /dashboards/serving/latency-regional, /dashboards/gpu/pools, /dashboards/observability/trace-samples

FAQ / Common pitfalls:
- Q: What if an experiment inadvertently affects private deployments?
  A: Immediately isolate network routes and notify Private Deployments lead; private deployments are excluded from default experiments.
- Q: Who can authorize a large-scope cross-region drill?
  A: Eng-Infra director + Eng-SRE lead signoff required.

Document maintenance and links:
- Owner must review this doc after any major fleet, autoscaler, or routing change.
- History: created 2024-11-05 by Maya R. Singh; reviewed and updated 2025-02-10 to add CI/CD canary template.

Appendix: Postmortem template (short):
1) Summary of experiment and outcome
2) Timeline of events and signals
3) Metrics before/during/after (attached charts)
4) Root cause / contributing factors
5) Action items, owners, ETA
6) Verification plan for each action

End of document.
